implementation_notes: Ruby's stdlib Thread::Queue#pop is thread-safe and hands each element to exactly one of several popping threads, so a fixed set of worker threads over one queue competes correctly inside a process; closing the queue makes blocked pops return nil and the workers exit. Threads buy concurrency for I/O-bound jobs but MRI's GVL denies CPU parallelism, which is why production Ruby scales the pattern with processes instead.
code_sketch:
queue = Thread::Queue.new
workers = n.times.map do
  Thread.new do
    while (job = queue.pop)     # each element goes to exactly one thread
      process(job)              # ack after success for broker-backed work
    end
  end
end
jobs.each { |j| queue << j }
queue.close
workers.each(&:join)
pitfalls: The GVL serialises CPU-bound work: threads do not use multiple cores, so CPU-heavy jobs need processes (Sidekiq/Resque) rather than more threads.
Thread::Queue#pop blocks forever on an open, empty queue - close it on shutdown or workers never finish.
An exception in a worker thread can vanish into Thread.abort_on_exception=false; supervise threads and requeue or record the failure explicitly.

variants.name: Sidekiq processes on one Redis queue (production form)
variants.idiom_name: Sidekiq processes on one Redis queue (production form)
variants.implementation_notes: The production realization: several Sidekiq worker processes subscribe to the same Redis-backed queue(s) and each process runs its threads concurrently, so competition spans processes and hosts; Resque is the process-per-job variant, and Bunny/karafka consumers the broker equivalents. The pattern code is the job class, and the queue - with retries, scheduled sets and dead sets - is the library's responsibility, which is exactly what makes this the default choice over hand-rolled Thread::Queue pools.
variants.code_sketch:
class SendEmailJob
  include Sidekiq::Job
  sidekiq_options queue: 'emails', retry: 5

  def perform(user_id)
    return if already_sent?(user_id)   # redelivery is normal: stay idempotent
    send_email(user_id)
  end
end
# scale: run more `bundle exec sidekiq -q emails` processes / more pods
pitfalls: Sidekiq retries failed jobs by default: a job that dies after its side effect runs again, so idempotency or a dedupe key is mandatory.
Retry exhaustion moves the job to the dead set - without monitoring and a replay path that is a silent black hole.
Per-process concurrency multiplies Redis connections and database pool pressure; raising worker count without raising the DB pool causes checkout timeouts.
